probe.format_note: Single 9:16 film, 720x1280, 30 fps, 1302 frames (43.4 s video), container 43.53 s. Audio: HE-AAC stereo 44.1 kHz, continuous for the whole film (no silence of 0.4 s or more below -45 dB), mean -16.6 dB, peak -1.4 dB; narrated voice with a bed, not analysed for beats; third-party audio never reused.

mode.why: third-party film of unknown origin: borrow the motion language, caption/label system and look only, never its shots one by one, its subject, its copy or its figures (owner note); the reference is a narrated how-it-works explainer (cause → mechanism inside → effect → proof numbers → limit → CTA), so EXPLAINER fits; a hook/problem/solution package may still run as REEL in this style

ignored.why: the subject (a microwave-pulse cruise missile, its name, the air force, the test site and its year) and every Persian caption, tag, label and CTA line are third-party copy and claims; never reused as voice-over, on-screen text or story

the figures on the stat cards (a shot count per flight, a target count per hour) are third-party claims; only the stat-card design and its pop-in/fade-out motion are borrowed, our numbers come from the approved package
the photo card holds a real third-party photograph with a credit line; never reused. The card is a slot for the owner's own images (input/) or sourced visuals the package names, with their own credit
the end card's handle and share line belong to the third-party channel; our end uses the brand's own CTA and logo outro

the scenery and props (night town of white blocks, office with workers, server rack in a mesh cage, desert test site, tripod camera, the missile itself) are the reference's story; our scenes take their subjects from the voice-over and are only drawn in this rendering style
the audio track (voice and bed) is third-party; L2/L6 use our own voice and sound

method: ffprobe; ffmpeg contact sheets fps=2, 480 px, tile 4x3 (8 sheets, all viewed); scene detect gt(scene,0.3) and gt(scene,0.12) (cuts at 3.13, 7.13, 10.23, 14.17, 15.47, 16.87-17.07 push-through, 18.07, 21.83, 23.23, 25.67, 29.63, 35.57, 39.93; 19.93 is an in-shot push, max score 0.80 at 35.57); dense sheets fps=10 over 2.8-3.6 s and 16.6-17.4 s, fps=5 over 32.4-34.0 s (all viewed). Spans from scene detect where a cut exists, otherwise from the sheets (about ±0.25 s). silencedetect + volumedetect on the audio. Colours read by eye, not sampled.

visual_language: Narrated 3D explainer in simple low-poly, flat-shaded models (boxes, cylinders, basic figures), cut like a documentary: 15 shots in 43.5 s, average about 2.9 s (range 1.1-4.4 s), almost all hard cuts placed on caption phrase changes, plus one forward push-through, one glow bloom and one foreground wipe. The story moves outside → inside → effect → proof → limit: establishing aerial, street level, hero close-up with proof card, x-ray cutaway, wide link shot, interior, abstract energy path, wireframe x-ray, blackout, intact contrast, aerial callback with stat, daylight test, close-up, barrier, end card. The invisible force is always drawn the same way (cyan rings / glow), so it reads across every set. Typography is a full on-screen system: (1) a bottom caption pill (dark translucent rounded box at about 85% height, bold Persian sans, 2-4 words per phrase, karaoke highlight: spoken words white, coming words grey, the current word underlined); (2) a small top chapter-tag pill at about 14% height with a coloured status dot (red = problem/effect, blue = explanation, green = safe/limit, orange = numbers/proof) that swaps with each chapter; (3) callout labels — dark small box with a coloured edge bar on the right and a thin leader line to a dot on the object, optional grey kicker over a bold name; (4) stat cards — dark rounded card, big orange digits + white unit word, grey sub line, orange edge bar; (5) a photo card for a real image with a credit chip. Moves: smooth, mostly linear camera drifts and slow push-ins; UI pops are short scale-ups with a slight overshoot (about 0.25-0.3 s) and fades out (about 0.3 s); effects travel continuously (rings, waves, orbs). Palette: deep navy night with cool white models and warm window light, cyan as the force colour, warm orange glows; daylight beige/pale blue for the proof chapter. Signature moments: rings sweeping through and every light going out at once; the push-through a ring into the hidden wiring; the x-ray wireframe world; the barrier the rings cannot pass.
look: Real 3D (not flat), low-poly and flat-shaded with clean bevel-free edges, matte materials (no texture detail except a speckled ground), a few translucent shells (cutaway tube) and emissive lines (light tubes, wireframe edges, traces). Light: cool moonlit night with a soft key, emissive windows and street lamps with bloom halos, warm exhaust glow, cyan energy glows with strong bloom; one bright daylight chapter with soft haze and aerial perspective. Shadows soft and subtle. Depth: real perspective, moderate depth of field (near roofs and foreground blocks blurred), motion blur on the push-through and the foreground wipe, distance haze on mountains. Background: navy gradient sky with a few stars and dark mountain silhouettes; pale blue sky and beige plain in daylight; pure black for the abstract and wireframe layers.
code_translation: Built as real 3D in code with three.js (D55), never flattened: low-poly BoxGeometry/CylinderGeometry models with flatShading MeshStandardMaterial in matte finish; emissive window planes and lamp sprites run through an UnrealBloomPass; a hemisphere + soft directional moonlight with soft shadows; fog for distance haze; depth of field as a blur pass (BokehPass) on near objects. The force effect: TorusGeometry rings with an additive emissive cyan material, scaled and faded along a path (instanced, staggered); the travelling wave as an animated emissive shader line; the orb as an additive sprite moving along a CatmullRom curve. X-ray layer: EdgesGeometry / LineSegments in glowing white over black, ghost figures in transparent cyan. Cutaway: MeshPhysicalMaterial with transmission/opacity for the shell. Push-through: fast camera dolly with frame-blend motion blur and a short additive cyan flash. Mesh barrier: thin cylinder grid or a wireframe box. All text is HTML/canvas overlay in the brand Persian font, never 3D-extruded: caption pill with word-by-word highlight synced to audio.json word times, chapter-tag pill with status dot, callout labels with leader lines projected from 3D anchor points (Vector3.project) each frame, stat cards with Persian digits per data-viz.md, photo card that holds the owner's input images unedited.
continuity: One visible sign for the invisible force: the same cyan rings/glow appear in every set, so the cause is readable across all cuts.
Outside → inside → effect: each chapter goes one layer deeper (aerial, street, room, cable, wiring, component) and then back out.
Push-through into the hidden layer: the camera rushes forward through the effect itself (a ring) with motion blur and a flash into the next world.
Same set, two states: a place is shown working, then the same place switched off or dark, so the change of state carries the explanation.
X-ray switch: the same room re-rendered as glowing wireframe to reveal what is inside the walls, then a push into one component.
Callback shot: the opening aerial returns later with a stat card on it, closing the loop between the hook and the proof.
Chapter tag with status colour: a small top pill changes text and dot colour at each chapter (problem, explanation, safe/limit, proof), a steady map of where the story is.
Labels anchored in space: callouts are tied by leader lines to points on 3D objects and follow them as the camera moves.
Karaoke captions: one bottom pill carries the voice word by word for the whole film, the only always-on element.
Day/night shift marks a change of chapter (night story → daylight proof).
Foreground wipe: an object sliding past the lens turns the wide into the next close-up without a cut.
Glow bloom to cut: the effect brightens into a halo that fills the frame just before the next shot.
Hero under the end card: the main actor keeps moving behind a darkened CTA card at the end.
risks: Third-party film of unknown origin: ADAPT only. Never copy its subject (a weapon), its town/office/server/test-site sets as designs, any caption, tag or label copy, its figures, its photo, its handle, its audio, or its shot order one by one.
Subject sensitivity: the reference explains a military weapon; our film's subject comes only from the voice-over, and the ring/force language must not make a non-military topic look like an attack.

Caption pill is small (cap height about 2% of frame height at 720 px) and the tag pill text even smaller: in our film both must meet the minimum sizes, contrast and safe zones (bottom caption above the platform UI band); Persian must be shaped and joined, never letter-split by the word highlight.
Too many text layers at once (caption + tag + label + stat card): L5 keeps at most one label or card besides the caption per beat and gives each the readability hold time.
Stat cards pop with a figure: every number must come from the approved package, land and hold, Persian digits per data-viz.md.

r1-s3's photo card holds a real photograph (counted as not code-buildable); in our film it is filled only with the owner's input images or credited sources from the package, never generated look-alikes of real photos.

Colours were read by eye: night navy, cyan force colour, orange stat accent and status-dot colours map onto brand colour roles (background, accent, positive/negative), never the literal reference colours.
Low-poly human figures appear; draw new generic figures only if the voice-over is about people, never trace the reference's.
Audio is third-party narration and bed; ignored, L6 builds the sound.
